clue.text: Suave Clark about Boris's leader – "drivel!"

indicators.note: about means going round, so the actor's surname wraps around the other piece
a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: Clark Gable, the smooth Hollywood leading man
the initial of Boris

explanation.surface: A smooth operator dismisses something Boris Johnson's leadership said as drivel.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Gable was the Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind, famed for his smooth charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To gabble is to talk rapidly and unintelligibly, which amounts to spouting nonsense.

clue.text: Green party's after one plain-spoken non-Latin

indicators.note: after places the party word at the end, behind the other pieces
non- negates, so the letter standing for Latin must be absent

blocks.note: one as the indefinite article
outspoken, forthright
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: The Green Party is portrayed as a blunt-talking outfit that has dropped Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: A + VOCA(L) + DO = AVOCADO. 'Green party' looks like the political party, but 'Green' alone is the definition and the party is a do.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is the name of a dull yellowish-green colour, taken from the fruit's flesh.

clue.text: It involves waxing a bit off knob's head

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of knob

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of a depilation session taking a bit off an intimate part.
explanation.walkthrough: The waxing suggests hair removal, but it is the wax used to resist dye on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is an Indonesian dyeing technique in which wax is applied to cloth to keep chosen areas free of colour.

clue.text: Woman needs resistance with party member getting fresh all the time

a member of the Green Party

explanation.surface: A woman joining the Green Party feels perpetually invigorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evergreen never loses its leaves or appeal, staying lively and current year after year.

clue.text: Diana sexist (some would say) with un-PC European hair

blocks.note: Hun is an offensive old name for a German
a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A goddess is accused of sexism alongside a politically incorrect foreigner's hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt; the gendered -ess ending is what 'some would say' is sexist.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, Roman goddess of hunting, is called the divine huntress, a feminine form some regard as needlessly gendered.

clue.text: House's after-effects after Clegg finally kicked out

kicked out means thrown out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the after-effects of heavy drinking
the closing letter of Clegg

explanation.walkthrough: HAN(G)OVER loses its G. 'House' reads like Parliament but is a royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover is the German royal dynasty that ruled Britain from George I to Victoria.

clue.text: (& 27ac.) Yes, Dave, "rien" negotiated – keep going!

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

the head of a word is its first letter

the opening letter of News

clue.text: Dynasty about to rise up between two extremes, which goes a long way in Ireland

between puts the pieces inside the two outer letters

south and north, the opposite poles of the compass

explanation.walkthrough: S(HAN + NO)N: the compass points are the two extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland, flowing for over three hundred kilometres.

clue.text: (& 21ac.) Honour presenter who ballsed up pie-in-the-sky future for Manchester etc

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

clue.text: Gross bit of vagina Virginia got rid of before tabloid's backlash

indicators.note: got rid of says the state abbreviation is removed from the preceding word

a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' looks like a comment on the anatomy, but it is the definition; a rag is a disparaging name for a tabloid newspaper.

This reveals all the ins and outs

blocks.clueFragment: Formal response by HSBC, say, to misconduct allegations?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first reading is a whimsical literal one.

clue.text: (&23ac.) Cabinet minister with armed service crew and Tory chief support, which Boris apparently lacks

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so each following piece is added on

the opening letter of Tory

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet minister' looks like the definition; it is just GOVE. Boris Johnson was then out of office.
explanation.definitionFit: At the time Johnson held no ministerial office, so an official job in the administration was precisely what he lacked.
